chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Doll Hutcherson and her daughter
summary: Danny recalls the woman trumpeter Doll Hutcherson, and chatting up her daughter who also played.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Because she was in the band with that woman...you know, that woman who played a helluva trumpet, had a daughter who played -- Doll.
Doll. Well, they had this woman band at one time, it was a helluva band, in vaudeville. And Fletcher's wife...

Yeah. She had this little daughter. I used to hit on all of them, and she'd say, 'Leave me alone. You're not my type of man.' 'I like you.' Hit on her (?). 'Why don't you leave me alone?' I'd annoyed her. She went to Philadelphia, got pregnant, and started making a whole lot of babies. Mmm! Little Doll. She could play.
I don't remember her daughter too well.
I remember she was married to a guy named Hutch who was a tenor saxophone player around Chicago. Hutcherson, a little short guy.
